title: The Power of Nutraceuticals in Skincare - DermLetter
abstract:
## Understanding Skin Aging  
The aging process affects the skin in various ways, leading to issues such as loss of elasticity, wrinkles, fine lines, loss of moisture, and discoloration. As we age, the performance of skin cells called fibroblasts deteriorates, resulting in reduced collagen synthesis and a loss of moisture. However, lifestyle choices and proper skincare can help minimize the signs of aging and maintain a smoother, more youthful appearance.  
Collagen, elastin, and proteoglycans are essential molecules for maintaining skin elasticity and resistance. Collagen, in particular, provides the skin with its firm structure. While topical collagen is known for its temporary effects on wrinkle reduction, ingestible collagen offers a way to replenish the natural supply that depletes with age. Ingredients like VERISOL, comprised of natural collagen peptides, have been specifically developed to enhance collagen metabolism and improve skin elasticity from the inside.
Clinical studies have demonstrated the positive effects of VERISOL on skin elasticity and wrinkle reduction. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, women aged 35-55 who received VERISOL collagen peptides showed a statistically significant improvement in skin elasticity compared to the placebo group. The positive impact on skin elasticity was more pronounced in women aged 50 years and older. Another study verified the efficacy of VERISOL in reducing eye wrinkle volume, with significant improvement observed after supplementation.
## Protection Against Sun Damage  
One of the most significant threats to the skin is ultraviolet radiation (UVR) from the sun. Sun exposure can lead to photoaging, immune dysfunction, inflammation, and even skin cancer. While sunscreen is essential, dietary supplements can offer additional support in protecting the skin from sun damage. Supplementation with ingredients like Lyc-O-Derm, derived from whole fruit tomato extract and carnosic acid, has been shown to enhance skin health, reduce UV-related skin damage, and protect DNA from photo-damage.  
Studies have also suggested that topical creams alone may not offer sufficient protection against sun damage. Most people do not apply enough sunscreen, resulting in inadequate protection. By incorporating digestible skin care technology into the daily diet, individuals can reduce molecular markers of photo-aging, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Nutraceuticals like Lyc-O-Derm provide a dietary approach to UV absorption and intracellular control of oxidative stress, promoting whole-body, endogenous photo-protection.
